sections.sustainability: Tu is a founding retailer in The Circuit (announced 23 Sept with New Look, M&S, Oxfam and Circle-8), a UK post-consumer textile recovery and automated-sorting initiative feeding fibre-to-fibre recyclers. Phase one starts January 2027 at Oxfam's Batley site; Tu MD Ben Smith framed it as 'learning and testing practical solutions'. AW26 also carries Tu's first recycled down-and-feather puffer (£85). No new Plan for Better clothing targets were published in the past 7 days.
sections.strategy: No Tu-specific corporate announcements in the past 7 days (latest Sainsbury's press releases, 22–28 Sept, cover Nectar, Sainsbury's Money and graduates). Ongoing direction under MD Ben Smith remains 'stretch up' premiumisation plus digital-first: trade press (Retail Gazette, 21 Sept) reports Tu womenswear digital sales are 1.5x two years ago, online up 20%+ and seven consecutive quarters of market outperformance, with phased monthly online drops replacing big seasonal launches. Next catalyst: H1 interim results, expected early November.
sections.pricing: AW26 price architecture (announced 9 Sept) holds value anchors — 86% of womenswear under £30 and 65% under £25, entry from £5 — while stretching the top end: lambswool from £34, mohair from £45, cashmere from £69, wool-blend coat and down puffer at £85. This is a deliberate good-better-best ladder aimed at M&S at the top while defending against George and F&F at the core.
sections.launches: October is the peak coat drop of AW26 womenswear: green hues, frogging detail and the main outerwear launch (Double-Faced Wool Blend Coat £85, waterproof parka £55, Denim Military Jacket £30). Knitwear range is 4x larger in premium fibres (merino, lambswool, cashmere, mohair, alpaca). November's drop moves to red, statement florals and embellished partywear.
sections.gossip: Trade press frames the supermarket fashion race as shifting online: Tesco is expanding F&F Online with more styles, sizes and online-exclusive edits, and George is leaning on influencer/ambassador partnerships, raising pressure on Tu's digital proposition. Consumer and YouTube haul coverage of Tu's AW26 'new in' is positive on the elevated look. No analyst notes specific to Tu surfaced this week.
soWhat: Tu's AW26 stretch into cashmere, mohair, alpaca, wool-blend and recycled down means premium-fibre knit and outerwear capability is now a buying criterion — suppliers with RWS/RAS/RDS and GRS-certified premium yarn or down supply chains should pitch SS27/AW27 programmes now, ahead of the post-interims buying cycle.

Monthly phased drops (Sept–Dec) and a digital-led model favour suppliers who can deliver smaller, staggered flows with reliable on-time-in-full performance; offering split shipments and shorter repeat lead times is a differentiator versus pure volume players.

The Circuit (live Jan 2027) signals future demand for recycled post-consumer fibre content and traceability reporting — suppliers should start building fibre-to-fibre recycled content options and material-level traceability data. Macro note: Bangladesh apparel exports to the UK rose 10.5% YoY in August, so Bangladesh capacity competition for UK programmes remains strong.
